With the tuned reference command, NEQ027 is still faster in current local Primo than tuned LLM2SMT, but the margin is much smaller. NEQ016 is a real tuned-LLM2SMT gap as well as a Z3 gap: tuned LLM2SMT solves locally in about 21.5s while Primo did not solve before interruption at 92s. The tuned reference did not use LLM2SMT's finite-domain value-precedence option for this improvement; the recorded tuned profile uses UF symmetry, four preprocessing passes, equality bridge, and EUF propagation thresholds.

entries.scope: Check whether the published primo.html NEQ023_size7 gap is consistent with local runs and stored artifacts
entries.command: Opened https://people.ciirc.cvut.cz/~janotmik/llm2smt/primo.html; ran build/primo --quiet --stats, --qf-uf-preprocess=basic, --no-uf-symmetry-breaking, --pure-theory-filter=auto; ran tuned LLM2SMT and local Z3 on tmp/QF_UF/NEQ/NEQ023_size7.smt2 with 60s timeout
entries.notes: The exact published primo2 number is worse than the current local build on this host, but the qualitative observation is consistent: NEQ023_size7 and nearby NEQ rows are substantially sensitive to Primo profile choices and remain slower than fast references. The no-symmetry ablation is much worse locally, while historical polarity/pure-auto artifacts show this family can improve substantially without solving the broader default-profile problem.

entries.command: Temporarily added --euf-decide=polarity, rebuilt build/primo, and ran build/primo --quiet --stats --euf-decide=polarity tmp/QF_UF/NEQ/NEQ023_size7.smt2 plus a small NEQ cluster smoke; reverted source after CaDiCaL aborted

references.name: LLM2SMT clean-room inspection
references.argv: /tmp/llm2smt source/docs inspected for cb_decide behavior only; no code copied

summary.prototype: --euf-decide=polarity returned unassigned-looking single-polarity theory atoms from OnlineEufPropagator::cb_decide
summary.abort: CaDiCaL fatal error: external decisions are only allowed over unassigned variables
summary.reason: CaDiCaL assignment notifications are not eager enough for the propagator's assignment_by_var_ map to prove that a candidate is currently unassigned at cb_decide time. A one-shot returned-variable guard still aborted, so other assigned observed variables can also be stale.
summary.api_check: CaDiCaL exposes is_decision(lit) but no safe in-callback unassigned query. val(lit) is SAT-model-only according to cadical.hpp and is not available during solving.
summary.source_status: prototype reverted; build/primo rebuilt and NEQ023_size7 solved normally in 4.88s after revert

entries.notes: Do not reintroduce EUF cb_decide without a synchronization design that can prove the returned literal is currently unassigned under CaDiCaL's delayed notification semantics, or without extending the SAT adapter with a supported assignment query. Current Primo remains limited to static theory phase plus EUF external conflicts/propagations for QF_UF SAT-search influence.

entries.scope: Compare Primo and tuned LLM2SMT preprocessing/stat shape on NEQ023_size7 after rejecting dynamic EUF decisions
entries.command: build/primo --quiet --stats tmp/QF_UF/NEQ/NEQ023_size7.smt2; /tmp/llm2smt/build/bin/llm2smt --quiet --stats --uf-symmetry-breaking --preprocess-passes 4 --eq-bridge --prop-interval 32 --prop-assign-threshold 0.25 --prop-delivery-budget 1000 tmp/QF_UF/NEQ/NEQ023_size7.smt2
entries.notes: On this representative NEQ row, the AMO gap is small and symmetry clause counts match. Tuned LLM2SMT has a larger SAT encoding but far fewer EUF assignments, so missing raw finite-domain AMO alone is unlikely to explain the remaining slowdown. The next likely levers are SAT search shape, phase/branching policy that is safe under CaDiCaL's callback semantics, or additional SAT-visible finite-domain/equality clauses beyond current AMO.

entries.scope: Compare Primo QF_UF option variants against tuned LLM2SMT and Z3 on a cheap NEQ cluster selected from the published primo.html gap table
entries.command: local loop over default, --finite-domain-equality-definitions, --ground-congruence, --theory-phase=polarity, combined eqdefs+phase, --qf-uf-preprocess=basic, tuned LLM2SMT, and z3; 30s timeout per run; CSV written to results/neq-cluster-option-matrix-local.csv

summary.interpretation: Finite-domain equality definitions did not fire on these NEQ files. Phase polarity is a selective SAT-search win, not a safe default from this evidence. Ground congruence remains too mixed for default use. Basic preprocessing is best for NEQ041_size8 but regresses the cluster aggregate.

entries.notes: Use this matrix as a SMAC/heuristic input, not as headline benchmark evidence. A promising next step is an opt-in auto phase mode guarded by cheap theory-atom polarity and finite-domain/symmetry statistics, then validate on the mixed QF_UF SMAC manifests before considering any default change.
